newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: GOLF-ROCCA AND TORRANCE FIGHT INJURIES.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-ROCCA AND TORRANCE FIGHT INJURIES.

text.p: Ryder Cup stalwarts Costantino Rocca and Sam Torrance battled injury problems in the Dutch Open on Thursday.
Italian Rocca's first round three-under-par 68, only two off the early pace, was his best for some weeks after he suffered a strained side.

Briton Torrance decided to play after a fitness-test on the range. The Scot's appearance was in doubt after he pulled a chest muscle in the gymnasium earlier in the week but he opted to play after morning treatment.
Australian Wayne Riley and Scot Paul Lawrie shared a one stroke lead on 66.

Two birdies in his last three holes put Rocca on the leaderboard for the first time since a run of injuries in June and July forced him out of the U.S. Open. Twice a member of Europe's team, he has now slipped from third to ninth in the Ryder Cup points table.

"I'm wearing an elastic support around my ribs on my side, which stops me turning freely," said Rocca. "But this was encouraging and if the injury continues to improve and I don't get any more injuries then maybe I can make the Ryder team."

Torrance, seeking his ninth successive appearance in the match against the Americans despite dropping to 13th on the list, said: "I've got to battle on because it's important for Ryder Cup points, but I'm in pain and there are going to be a lot of chip-shots out there."
